old: This was not because he was a coward -- far from it.
new: This was not because he was cowardly and abject -- quite the contrary.
reason: Source: 'not because he was cowardly and abject, quite the contrary'; 'abject' was dropped.

old: bordering on nervous collapse
new: bordering on hypochondria
reason: Source: 'verging on hypochondria' (a morbid, brooding state); 'nervous collapse' invents a different diagnosis.

old: thinking... about fairy tales.
new: thinking... about Jack the Giant-killer.
reason: Source: 'thinking... of Jack the Giant-killer'; the specific reference was flattened to 'fairy tales'.

old: he would realize that his thoughts were tangled
new: he would realize that his thoughts were sometimes tangled
reason: Source: 'his ideas were sometimes in a tangle'; the hedge 'sometimes' was dropped.

old: though he still did not fully admit this to himself
new: though he still did not realize this himself
reason: Source: 'although he still did not realise this himself'; 'did not fully admit' implies he half-knew, changing his self-awareness.

old: He was going now for a "rehearsal"
new: He was positively going now for a "rehearsal"
reason: Source: 'He was positively going now for a “rehearsal”'; 'positively' was dropped.

old: With his heart pounding and his hands trembling,
new: With a sinking heart and a nervous tremor,
reason: Source: 'With a sinking heart and a nervous tremor'; 'heart pounding' reverses the dread into excitement and 'hands trembling' is invented.

old: what would it be like if I were actually going to do it?
new: what would it be like if it somehow came to pass that I were really going to do it?
reason: Source: 'if it somehow came to pass that I were really going to do it'; the tentative 'somehow came to pass' was dropped.

old: God, how pathetic all this is!
new: Phew, how utterly petty it all is!
reason: Source: 'Phew, how utterly petty it all is!'; 'pathetic' shifts the dismissal (it is trivial) into self-pity.

old: Because in destitution I am the first to degrade myself.
new: Because in destitution I am ready to be the first to degrade myself.
reason: Source: 'in beggary I am ready to be the first to humiliate myself'; 'ready to be' was dropped.

old: He clearly had not undressed or washed in at least five days.
new: It seemed quite likely that he had not undressed or washed for the last five days.
reason: Source: 'It seemed quite probable that he had not undressed or washed for the last five days'; the narrator's surmise became a certainty and 'at least' is invented.

old: Tell me, young man -- no, let me put it more strongly and precisely:
new: Excuse me, young man, can you.... No, let me put it more strongly and precisely:
reason: Source: 'Excuse me, young man, can you.... No, to put it more strongly'; the broken-off 'can you....' self-correction was removed, which the following '_can_ you... _dare_ you' depends on.

old: Granted, I am a scoundrel,
new: Granted, granted, I am a scoundrel,
reason: Source: 'Granted, granted, I am a scoundrel'; Marmeladov's repetition dropped.

old: Honored sir, you see, every person
new: Honored sir, honored sir, you see, every person
reason: Source: 'Honoured sir, honoured sir, you know every man'; Marmeladov's repetition dropped.

old: Ivan Ivanovitch Klopstock
new: Ivan Ivanitch Klopstock
reason: Source form is 'Ivan Ivanitch Klopstock'.

old: she just picked up our big green _drap de dames_ shawl, covered
new: she just picked up our big green _drap de dames_ shawl (we have a shawl, made of _drap de dames_), covered
reason: Source keeps Marmeladov's rambling parenthesis '(we have a shawl, made of _drap de dames_)'.

old: in each other's arms... together... yes...
new: in each other's arms... together, together... yes...
reason: Source: 'together, together... yes'; the repetition was dropped.

old: 'it's better if I don't visit too often. Maybe after dark, when no one can see.' Do you hear that?
new: 'it's better if I don't visit too often. Maybe after dark, when no one can see.' Do you hear, do you hear?
reason: Source: 'Do you hear, do you hear?'; Marmeladov's repeated refrain was reduced.

old: led Semyon Zaharovitch by the hand into his private office.' Do you hear?
new: led Semyon Zaharovitch by the hand before everybody into his private office.' Do you hear, do you hear?
reason: Source: 'led Semyon Zaharovitch by the hand before everybody into his study.' Do you hear, do you hear?'; 'before everybody' (the boast's point) and the repetition were dropped.

old: -- do you hear? --
new: -- do you hear, do you hear? --
reason: Source: '(do you hear, do you hear;)'; repetition dropped.

old: I spent in blissful dreams
new: I spent in fleeting dreams
reason: Source: 'passed in fleeting dreams'; 'blissful' changes the image and loses the transience.

old: a certain practiced slyness and show of bravado
new: a certain put-on slyness and show of bravado
reason: Source: 'a certain assumed slyness and affectation of bravado'; 'assumed' means feigned, not practiced.

old: That's not something that happens on earth, but up there... up there they grieve over people,
new: Not on earth, but up there... they grieve over people,
reason: Source: 'Not on earth, but up yonder... they grieve over men'; the explanatory 'That's not something that happens on earth' and the repeated 'up there' are added.

old: And she probably needs them herself now
new: And maybe she needs them herself now
reason: Source: 'And maybe she needs them now'; 'probably' raises the certainty.

old: what all that smartness costs?
new: what all that smartness means?
reason: Source: 'what all that smartness means'; the phrase is echoed by Raskolnikov in 4.4, and 'costs' loses its moral sense.

old: crucify me -- but pity me while you do it!
new: crucify me, but pity me!
reason: Source: 'Crucify me, oh judge, crucify me but pity me!'; 'while you do it' is added.

old: the wretched drunkard, her earthly father, undaunted by his degradation
new: the filthy drunkard, her earthly father, undaunted by his beastliness
reason: Source: 'the filthy drunkard, her earthly father, undismayed by his beastliness'; softened, and 'beastliness' carries his 'I am a beast' motif.

old: And so on.
new: And so on, and so on.
reason: Source: 'And so on, and so on.'

old: he had obviously just been beaten
new: he had probably just been beaten
reason: Source: 'probably he had just had a beating'; 'obviously' raises the narrator's certainty.

old: threatening the poor woman for the hundredth time with eviction the next day
new: trying for the hundredth time to frighten the poor woman by ordering her, with coarse abuse, to clear out of the room the next day
reason: Source: 'for the hundredth time to frighten the poor woman by ordering her with coarse abuse to clear out of the room next day'; 'coarse abuse' was dropped.

old: laughing bitterly
new: laughing spitefully
reason: Source: 'he laughed malignantly'; 'bitterly' softens the malice.

old: He was in the grip of a fixation so total that everything else had fallen away.
new: He was in the state that overtakes some monomaniacs who are entirely concentrated on one thing.
reason: Source: 'He was in the condition that overtakes some monomaniacs entirely concentrated upon one thing'; the comparison to monomaniacs was dropped and 'everything else had fallen away' is added.

old: She was a country girl and very talkative.
new: She was a peasant woman from the country and very talkative.
reason: Source: 'She was a country peasant-woman and a very talkative one'; 'girl' changes her age and class.

old: "Don't bite the hand that feeds you."
new: "Don't turn your nose up at your bread and butter."
reason: Source: 'Don't quarrel with your bread and butter' (don't scorn your livelihood); 'bite the hand that feeds you' means ingratitude.

old: prayed with tears for the strength to bear
new: prayed with tears to Our Lady for the strength to bear
reason: Source: 'prayed with tears to Our Lady to give her strength'; the religious detail was dropped.

old: In every house she was expected before she arrived, and people gathered for each reading,
new: In every house she was expected before she arrived, and everyone knew that on such and such a day Marfa Petrovna would be reading the letter in such and such a place, and people gathered for each reading,
reason: Source: 'everyone knew that on such and such a day Marfa Petrovna would be reading the letter in such and such a place'; the clause was dropped.

old: A great deal of this was unnecessary, in my opinion,
new: In my opinion a great deal, a very great deal of this was unnecessary,
reason: Source: 'In my opinion a great deal, a very great deal of all this was unnecessary'; her emphatic repetition was dropped.

old: The poor madman was treated rather harshly.
new: It really was treating the crazy fellow too harshly.
reason: Source: 'it was really treating the crazy fellow too harshly'; 'rather' weakens 'too', and 'crazy fellow' matches her earlier phrase in this letter.

old: From many signs, Pyotr Petrovitch seems to be a thoroughly estimable man.
new: Pyotr Petrovitch, judging by many indications, is a thoroughly estimable man.
reason: Source: 'Pyotr Petrovitch, judging by many indications, is a thoroughly estimable man'; the added 'seems' hedges what she asserts.

old: that may simply be because he's a blunt man -- and that's probably all it is.
new: that may well come from his being an outspoken man -- and no doubt that's how it is.
reason: Source: 'that may well come from his being an outspoken man, and that is no doubt how it is'; her anxious self-reassurance ('no doubt') was weakened to 'probably'.

old: and ideally one who had experienced poverty, because, as he explained, a wife should not consider herself her husband's equal but should view him as her benefactor.
new: and, above all, one who had experienced poverty, because, as he explained, a man ought not to be indebted to his wife, and it is better for a wife to look upon her husband as her benefactor.
reason: Source: 'above all, one who had experienced poverty, because... a man ought not to be indebted to his wife, but that it is better for a wife to look upon her husband as her benefactor'; 'ideally' weakens 'above all', and 'not... her husband's equal' is invented.

old: some shop clerks
new: some shopkeepers and clerks
reason: Source: 'some shopmen and clerks' (two groups).

old: even before the Feast of Our Lady
new: even before the Fast of Our Lady
reason: Source: 'before the fast of Our Lady' (the Dormition fast, early August); a feast is a different date.

old: she has so much to tell you
new: she has so much, so much to tell you
reason: Source: 'she has so much, so much to tell you'; repetition dropped.

old: thought for a long time
new: brooded, brooded for a long time
reason: Source: 'pondered, pondered a long time'; repetition dropped.

old: no bigger than a cupboard, a coffin
new: like a cupboard or a box
reason: Source: 'the little yellow room that was like a cupboard or a box'; 'coffin' is an added image.

old: That _seems_ is everything!
new: That _seems_ beats everything!
reason: Source: 'That _seems_ beats everything!' (sarcastic: that tops it all); 'is everything' changes the sense.

old: Was it all spoken aloud,
new: Was it all put into _words_,
reason: Source: 'Was it all put into _words_'; italic emphasis lost.

old: he struck her as somewhat rude,
new: he struck her as rude, _a little_,
reason: Source: 'he struck her as rude _a little_'; his sarcastic italic on her understatement lost.

old: 'You are everything to us, our only comfort, our only hope.'
new: 'You are our one comfort, you are everything to us.'
reason: Source: '‘You are our one comfort, you are everything to us.’'; 'our only hope' is added to the quotation.

old: who expounds his theory that wives rescued from destitution should be forever grateful to their husbands
new: who expounds the theory that wives raised from destitution, who owe everything to their husband's generosity, are superior
reason: Source: 'propounds the theory of the superiority of wives raised from destitution and owing everything to their husband's bounty'; the theory is about such wives being preferable, not just grateful.

old: or a serf under a German master
new: or a Lett with a German master
reason: Source: 'a Lett with a German master' (Latvian peasants under Baltic German landlords); flattened to 'serf'. See report on the other half of this phrase.

old: That's exactly what's happening here, clear as day.
new: That's just like us, clear as day.
reason: Source: 'That's just like us, it's as clear as daylight'; the generalisation about 'us' became a claim about this case.

old: Have you both measured your sacrifice? Really measured it?
new: Have you both taken the measure of your sacrifice?
reason: Source: 'Have you taken the measure of your sacrifice, both of you?'; 'Really measured it?' is added.

old: So you'll have to 'keep up appearances' too. Do you understand what that means?
new: So you'll have to 'keep up appearances' too. Isn't that so? Do you understand what that smartness means?
reason: Source: 'Is not that so? Do you understand what that smartness means?'; the echo of Marmeladov's 'smartness' was lost.

old: It has to be paid for, Dounia, this kind of smartness.
new: It has to be paid for, it has to be paid for, Dounia, this kind of smartness.
reason: Source: 'It has to be paid for, it has to be paid for, Dounia'; repetition dropped.

old: It will not! I refuse!
new: It will not, it will not! I refuse!
reason: Source: 'it shall not, it shall not!'; repetition dropped.

old: even found a kind of perverse pleasure in it
new: even found a kind of pleasure in it
reason: Source: 'finding a kind of enjoyment in it'; 'perverse' is an added judgment.

old: Long ago his current anguish had begun.
new: Long, long ago his current anguish had begun.
reason: Source: 'Long, long ago his present anguish had its first beginnings'; repetition dropped.

old: now it appeared as something other than a dream entirely
new: now it seemed not a dream at all
reason: Source: 'now it appeared not a dream at all'; plainer faithful wording.

old: He, too, clearly wanted to approach the girl
new: He, too, apparently wanted to approach the girl
reason: Source: 'He, too, would apparently have liked to approach the girl'; 'clearly' raises the certainty.

old: if only she'd tell us where to take her. Miss!
new: if only she'd tell us where to take her, but as it is.... Miss!
reason: Source: 'if only she'd tell us where to take her, but as it is.... Missy'; trailing-off dropped.

old: In two or three years -- a wreck, dead at eighteen or nineteen....
new: In two or three years -- a wreck, her life over at eighteen or nineteen....
reason: Source: 'a wreck, and her life over at eighteen or nineteen'; 'dead' is not what the source says.

old: Haven't I seen cases like that? Every single one of them ended up that way.
new: Haven't I seen cases like that? And how did they get there? Why, they all came to it just like this.
reason: Source: 'And how have they been brought to it? Why, they've all come to it like that'; the rhetorical question was dropped and the point shifted.

old: But what if Dounia ends up as one of the percentage? Part of one, if not another?
new: But what if Dounia were one of the percentage! If not that one, then another?
reason: Source: 'But what if Dounia were one of the percentage! Of another one if not that one?'; the candidate's 'Part of one, if not another?' is hard to follow.

old: some hidden meaning
new: some sinister meaning
reason: Source: 'some sinister significance'; 'sinister' was dropped.

old: a thought came to him
new: a fantastic thought came to him
reason: Source: 'a fantastic thought came into his head'; 'fantastic' dropped.

old: as red as a beet
new: as red as a carrot
reason: Source: 'a fleshy face red as a carrot'; image changed.

old: like a felled tree
new: like a log
reason: Source: 'she fell on the ground like a log'; image changed.

old: and sat up in terror
new: and jumped up in terror
reason: Source: 'and stood up in terror'; the next paragraph has him 'sitting down under a tree', which needs him standing first.

old: Yesterday, when I went to do that... _experiment_
new: Yesterday, yesterday, when I went to do that... _experiment_
reason: Source: 'Yesterday, yesterday, when I went to make that... _experiment_'; repetition dropped.

old: She was a complete slave to her sister,
new: She was a complete slave and lived in fear and trembling of her sister,
reason: Source: 'She was a complete slave and went in fear and trembling of her sister'; the fear was dropped.

old: Raskolnikov had just passed by and heard every word.
new: Raskolnikov had just passed by and heard no more.
reason: Source: 'Raskolnikov had just passed and heard no more'; 'heard every word' reverses the source.

old: the old woman whose life he was contemplating would be home
new: the old woman on whose life an attempt was planned would be home
reason: Source: 'an old woman, on whose life an attempt was contemplated'; 'whose life he was contemplating' loses the sense of an attempt on her life.

old: who was leaving for Harkov
new: who had since left for Harkov
reason: Source: 'who had left for Harkov'; chronology.

old: She's rich as a Rothschild
new: She's as rich as a Jew
reason: Source: 'She is as rich as a Jew'; period language was softened. Restored per protocol F7.

old: whom the nasty creature constantly beat
new: whom the wretched little creature constantly beat
reason: Source: 'whom the wretched little creature was continually beating'; 'little' (the contrast with the six-foot Lizaveta) was dropped.

old: even though Lizaveta was nearly six feet tall
new: even though Lizaveta was at least six feet tall
reason: Source: 'though Lizaveta was at least six feet high'; 'nearly' reverses the degree.

old: Dozens of families saved from poverty, ruin, depravity, disease -- all with her money.
new: Dozens of families saved from destitution, from ruin, from vice, from the venereal hospitals -- all with her money. For one life, thousands would be saved from corruption and decay.
reason: Source: 'from the Lock hospitals--and all with her money... For one life thousands would be saved from corruption and decay'; the specific reference was flattened to 'disease' and the whole 'For one life thousands would be saved' sentence was dropped. (Moved within this paragraph only.)

old: I was just arguing the principle of the thing....
new: I was just arguing the justice of it....
reason: Source: 'I was only arguing the justice of it'; the officer's reply in 6.20 ('there's no justice in it') echoes this word.

old: as though something had been lying in wait, something preordained, some guiding hint....
new: as though there had really been something preordained in it, some guiding hint....
reason: Source: 'as though there had really been in it something preordained, some guiding hint'; 'lying in wait' is imported from 5.63.

old: he muttered as he passed through the gateway
new: he thought as he passed through the gateway
reason: Source: 'he reflected, as he went under the gateway'; he thinks this, he does not say it.

old: Ringing further was pointless and would attract attention.
new: Ringing further was pointless and out of place.
reason: Source: 'To go on ringing was useless and out of place'; 'would attract attention' is an added motive.

old: stood out in his memory with terrifying clarity, forever.
new: stood out in his memory vividly, distinctly, forever.
reason: Source: 'that moment stood out in his mind vividly, distinctly, for ever'; 'terrifying' is added.
